svg.title: The failure-to-recovery timeline of an internet edge and four scenarios compared without and with an edge design
svg.desc: A timeline from zero seconds to thirty seconds and beyond, marked with link failure, BFD or carrier detection, route or exit switch, session rebuild and the user retrying or calling. A comparison table lists four scenarios: the primary link physically failing, where without design BGP waits for its 180 second hold timer while with design BFD is sub-second and sessions rebuild within five seconds; the link staying up while the path is broken, where without design the interface stays up and traffic enters a black hole for forty minutes while with design IP SLA or BFD watches end to end and withdraws the route; the primary ISP dropping half its prefixes, where the BGP session stays up and nobody notices; and a stateful device failing first, where both exits are up but every session dies. A footer asks for a detection budget and a recovery budget in the design document.
svg.text: Thirty seconds after the primary exit fails: who sees what
The design question is not whether you have two ISPs. It is what the user experiences between the failure and the recovery.
THE TIMELINE EVERY EDGE DECISION HAS TO ANSWER
the only interval that can be designed:
detection + switch, not the application's retry timer
WITH THE EDGE DESIGNED FOR IT

text.class: BGP hold 180 s 才切；用户先报障
BFD sub-second，会话在 5 s 内重建
接口 up → 路由仍优选 → 流量进洞 40 min
IP SLA / BFD 看端到端，主动撤路由

svg.text: 主 ISP 丢了一半前缀

text.class: BGP 会话还在 → 没人发现
前缀监控 + 备用出口的等价宣告
两台出口都在，会话全断
会话同步 / 非状态化设计 / 快速清表

svg.text: Two numbers to write into the design document
Detection budget: how long until the edge knows the path is gone (BFD 300 ms x 3, BGP hold 180 s by default, IP SLA probe interval).
Recovery budget: how long until a user-visible session works again (route switch + NAT rebinding + firewall session + application retry).
Deploying two ISPs without writing these two budgets is how a redundant design still produces a 40-minute outage.
